inputs.prompt: Visual development reference for an artistic 3D scene-investigation demo, not a real forensic record. Single wide cinematic view of a generic anonymous human-shaped reconstruction next to a complete tubular metal chair in a dark sparse scanned room. Full human silhouette visible from head to both feet with generous framing; human and chair plausibly scaled together. Abstract matrix material: tiny ordered cyan and teal square pixels, sparse luminous contour strands, hollow-square inferred surface marks, subtle horizontal quantization, generous dark negative space through the body. Readable gesture with one hand gently reaching toward the chair. Not a solid mannequin: no opaque white glowing body, no overexposure, no noisy particle explosion, no code rain, no text, no logos, no weapons, no blood, no victim. Both chair and figure have coherent 3D form; artistic pixel breakup is a surface treatment not missing geometry. Quiet museum-installation aesthetic. Static reference for implementing a native real-time shader; not a photorealistic reconstructed event.

runs.inspection: Full image inspected: hollow-square cyan pixels, broken contours, restrained luminance and full-body framing. Select material/framing only; generic cantilever chair is not source geometry.

inputs.prompt: Animate this artistic reference as a quiet native 3D reconstruction demo. Locked wide camera, entire anonymous pixel human visible head to feet throughout, generous top and bottom margin. Over ten seconds: hold still briefly, smoothly lean a little toward the chair while the right arm gently reaches toward its back, ease to a brief rest, smoothly retract the arm and return to the initial standing pose, then hold. Smooth physically restrained transitions with stable feet and no sliding; no sudden pose snapping. Preserve sparse cyan/teal square-pixel contours and dark negative space; pixels are anchored to the moving body rather than random flashing or glitter. Chair remains still and complete throughout, no collision, no falling, no violent action, no inferred historical event. No camera orbit, zoom, jump cuts, white glowing solid surfaces, strobe, text, captions, interface, logo or audio. A non-evidentiary motion design reference; preserve generic identity and room composition.

runs.inspection: Full ffmpeg decode passed. Lead inspected 40 chronological samples at 4 fps: slow lean, extended pause, return; sparse contours, fixed chair, almost fixed feet and camera. Not real-time viewing or a performance measurement. Initial headroom is too tight; implementation must retain more margin.
